summary: ApolloHealth: conversation state inconsistency across replicas causing incorrect patient summaries and SLA breach - follow-up
description:
Issue summary: During a morning traffic spike on 2026-03-05 ApolloHealth reported that their clinical-summary assistant returned inconsistent patient summaries for the same conversation session. Some completions omitted recently provided context and in one case combined content from unrelated sessions. This produced incorrect triage suggestions and violated ApolloHealth's SLA (95th percentile latency and correctness guarantee).

Reported impact: incorrect patient summaries in production, multiple customer-facing misclassifications, and an SLA credit request.

Initial customer-reported symptoms: session X returned an earlier cached summary while session Y returned newly appended clinical notes; both queries used same session_id and conversation_id in client logs.
impact: Affecting 1.8% of ApolloHealth requests between 07:22–08:05 UTC in us-east-1. Observed incorrect completions for ~24 unique patient sessions; 3 customers escalated to Apollo's security/compliance team. SLA 95th-percentile latency breached and functional correctness violations reported.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use ApolloHealth account credentials and simulate conversation with session_id=ap-h-<seed>.
2) Send a sequence of messages that append a new clinical note and ask for an updated summary.
3) Trigger a parallel request to the same session_id routed to a different replica (force by changing origin IP to simulate multi-edge routing).
4) Observe that one replica returns summary without appended note while the other includes it; occasionally responses mix fragments from unrelated sessions.
logs: Key logs: session-coordinator: WARN session-affinity-mismatch for session_id=ap-h-9e3 (07:26:13). serving-runtime: ERROR kv-cache-denormalization detected for model=redwood-chat-7B (07:26:14). autoscaler: info added replica r-az2-14 (07:25:59); routing: debug routed request to r-az2-14 (07:26:12). Stack traces show fast restart of replica r-az2-14 and cache warmup. Full log excerpts saved to S3: s3://redwood-support/apollohealth/SUP-981234/logs-20260305.tgz
investigation_notes: First responder (Support) validated client logs and asked for sample request IDs to correlate: client provided reqs 78a1, 78a4, 78b0.
SRE replicated traffic in staging with same autoscaler behavior and reproduced mismatch when autoscaler spawned a new replica while in-flight requests were being forwarded.

Hypothesis A: new replica handled a request before KV-prefetch completed leading to missing prefix context. Hypothesis B: session-affinity header was intermittently dropped by edge router causing two different replicas to handle sequential messages.
Correlation found between autoscaler replica addition and session-affinity expiration TTL of 60s — requests that hit newly added replica saw stale/no KV cache state for the session.
Telemetry: 98% of mismatches occurred within 30s of a replica lifecycle event (start/stop); tails aligned with autoscaler events in us-east-1 AZs.
findings: Root cause: race between autoscaler and session-affinity/cache-warmup. New replicas accepted traffic prior to completing KV prefix population for live sessions. The routing layer allowed session-affinity to fall back to best-effort routing after affinity TTL expired; combined with fast replica joins this produced cross-session KV cache reads that manifested as missing context or interleaved fragments. Secondary factor: default affinity TTL (60s) and cache warmup latency (~5–12s) were not coordinated.
resolution:
Short-term: applied emergency rollback to autoscaler scaling policy for ApolloHealth's dedicated pools (disabled reactive scale-ups for 10 minutes) and increased session-affinity TTL to 300s for the customer's routing policy, preventing mid-session reroutes. We also implemented a gate in serving-runtime: replica will reject requests for known session_ids until KV prefix warmup completes (feature flag ff/kv-warmup-gate enabled for ApolloHealth).

Long-term: engineering PR to modify autoscaler and routing handshake to ensure replica readiness signal is only returned after KV cache warmup and session-affinity handoff confirmed. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/15432 (merged 2026-03-11).

Customer communication: support sent an incident summary and remediation timeline on 2026-03-06; SLA credit offer and compliance evidence delivered on 2026-03-10.
followup_actions: ENG-1: Instrument warmup-ready metric and add healthcheck gating to routing (owner: @ethan-brooks, ETA: 2026-03-18).
ENG-2: Lower default affinity TTL configurable per-customer and document tradeoffs (owner: @maria-gonzales, ETA: 2026-03-22).
OPS-1: Add automated canary for replica-join warmup behavior and alert when in-flight requests routed to non-warm replicas (owner: @sre-oncall, ETA: 2026-03-15).
CS-1: Follow up with ApolloHealth compliance to confirm acceptance of evidence package and closure of their audit request (owner: @maya-chen, ETA: 2026-03-12).
DOC-1: Update runbook for session-affinity incidents and include steps for temporary policy adjustments (owner: @docs-team, ETA: 2026-03-19).
